Hi Karthik,

Confirmed on the sizing: steady-state 8 A100-equivalent GPUs, with two short daily peaks where we'd need capacity at ~16-equivalent for up to 90 minutes each. Throughput: target is 400r/min, p95 target is 800–1,000ms (we can accept a little flexibility there but need to document expectations).

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated/private tenancy pricing info request — Helios initial sizing (engineering notes)

Karthik / Marissa,

Quick engineering/packaging notes based on Sara's sizing. I'm keeping numbers high-level; we should flag these as estimates until infra confirms exact SKU mapping.

1) Mapping & burst: 8 steady-state A100-equivalents maps to an 8-GPU committed pool. For the daily 90m spikes to 16-equivalent we recommend reserving burst headroom via a 2x burst policy (63% of the time you'll be on steady, with auto-burst to capacity within policy). Burst will be charged per-minute at the committed hourly rate when used — we typically price burst usage as variable billing on top of the base commit.

2) Isolation pricing model (how we typically break it out):
- Base reserved commit: monthly fee tied to GPU pool size and expected token/throughput.
- Single-tenant isolation premium: recurring surcharge (our standard model) — we typically set this as 15–22% of the base commit depending on the isolation level (network sequester, dedicated infra, extra tracing). For healthcare with long log retention and KMS, plan on the higher end (18% baseline).
- KMS integration: two components — one-time integration/setup ($12,000) + ongoing key-management & audit access fee ($1,800/month). If they want HSM-backed keys or dedicated HSM connector we need a separate procurement line (est. $8k one-time).
- Audit-log retention: first 90 days included, then tiered storage fees. For 3-year searchable retention we estimate $1,250/month (indexing + storage + support) for Helios' expected volume; can be packaged into the commit for a fixed fee if preferred.

3) SLA and credits: for Dedicated we offer 99.9% availability target with financial credits tiered (0.5–10% of monthly bill depending on severity/agreed SLO misses). Latency SLOs are handled with routing and capacity policies — we can define p95 targets in the SLA but credits are availability-first.

4) Packaging proposals (ballpark ARR-levels assuming current public pricing lines):
- Pilot (3mo): base commit for 8 GPUs, no long-term discount, isolation premium + setup fees waived only if they move to 12mo. Estimated monthly: $48,000 base + 18% isolation premium (~$8,640) + audit retention $1,250 + KMS monthly $1,800 = ~$59,690/mo.
- Standard 12mo commit: 10% discount on base commit, isolation premium at 18% recurring, KMS integration one-time fee waived for >=12mo at our discretion. Estimated monthly after discount: $43,200 base (after 10% on $48k) + $7,776 isolation + $1,250 audit + $1,800 KMS = ~$53,  ~26k? (note: I'll produce a cleaned table for customer-facing doc).
- Enterprise 36mo commit: 15–18% discount on base, isolation premium at 15% recurring, KMS setup waived, multi-year pricing for audit retention can be amortized to lower monthly.

I'll produce a customer-friendly pricing table and separate the one-time vs recurring lines. We should decide if legal needs to block any specific language on KMS/HSM.

-- Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Dedicated/private tenancy pricing info request — Helios initial sizing (pricing guidance)

Karthik — quick commercial guidance:

- Offer a 12-month commit at a 10% discount on the base commit (standard play).
- Apply an 18% recurring isolation surcharge for the SOC2 + 3yr retention + KMS requirements.
- Waive the $12k KMS integration fee if they sign the 12mo at a minimum $180k ARR (or equivalent monthly commit).
- For SLA: offer standard 99.9% availability with credits up to 10% of monthly fee for qualifying downtime. No need to put aggressive latency credits in the first pass — handle latency with routing commitments.

If procurement pushes too hard, we can move to 12% discount for 12mo or fold audit retention into a fixed monthly line to simplify contracting.

Marissa
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
